title: New Orleans Saints turn to rookie Jonas Sanker after Julian Blackmon's injury - NewsBreak
text:
By Sara Palczewski ,
13 hours ago
METAIRIE, La. (Louisiana First) — The New Orleans Saints are once again scrambling at safety with Julian Blackmon out long-term with a shoulder injury. The black and gold first brought Blackmon in shortly after Tyrann Mathieu surprisingly retired right before training camp.
Replacing him won’t be easy. Blackmon played every defensive snap against Arizona and was one of the highest-graded Saints players in that game.
The Saints will turn to rookie Jonas Sanker to replace Blackmon, with others rotating in.
Saints head coach Kellen Moore said Sanker will do an “awesome job”. The third-round pick played just one defensive snap against Arizona but impressed in preseason and training camp with his physical play style.
“Certainly, his physicality that he plays with, but I think he plays it in a manner that is still sound,” Moore said. “He’s not reckless. I thought he had a ton of examples through preseason football where he showed up in the team meetings every week because of these big, physical, aggressive plays. He’s doing it in a very patient, sound way. He’s just got to stay there.”
“His story follows my story,” Saints safety Justin Reid said. “My rookie year, I started the second game of the season for the same reason that there was an injury that came up in the first game, and I started the second game of the season. So, I already talked to Jonas just a little bit about that, and he’ll be ready for the moment. He shined in preseason, just flying around all over the ball, and we just need that same player to play on Sunday, and his best will be good enough for us.”
Moore said Blackmon will have surgery this week on his injured shoulder.
